title.en: Moroccan police arrest more than 100 people as they attempt to enter Ceuta
title.zh: 摩洛哥警方逮捕逾百名试图进入休达者

summary.en: Moroccan police arrested 111 individuals attempting to enter Spain's North African territory of Ceuta. This action followed tightened border security measures on both sides, prompted by social media calls for a mass crossing.
summary.zh: 摩洛哥警方逮捕了111名试图进入西班牙北非属地休达的人。此前，社交媒体上呼吁进行大规模越境，导致双方边境安全措施收紧。

body.en: Border security tightened after social media posts call for another mass crossing into Spain’s north African territory Moroccan police have arrested 111 people as they tried to enter Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta, amid ⁠tightened security on both sides after social media posts ​called for another mass crossing. The attempted crossing on Saturday came two weeks after more than 72,000 migrants surged into Ceuta , causing tensions within the EU and prompting anti-immigration rhetoric among far-right parties worldwide. At least 96 people died trying to ⁠reach European soil. Continue reading...
body.zh: 社交媒体帖子呼吁再次大规模越境进入西班牙北非领土后，边境安全收紧摩洛哥警方逮捕了 111 名试图进入西班牙北非领土休达的人，社交媒体帖子呼吁再次大规模越境后，双方安全都加强了。两周前，超过 72,000 名移民涌入休达，引发欧盟内部紧张局势，并引发世界各地极右翼政党的反移民言论。至少 96 人在试图到达欧洲土地的过程中丧生。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news reminds us of the ancient call to treat those seeking refuge or a new home with dignity and compassion. Yahweh's command to Israel, having once been foreigners themselves, was to love the stranger as one's own. Even amidst complex border challenges, this principle invites us to consider the humanity of all who seek a better life.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻提醒我们，要以尊严和怜悯对待寻求庇护或新家园的人。雅伟曾命令以色列民，因他们自己也曾是寄居的，要爱寄居的如同爱自己。即使面对复杂的边境挑战，这一原则也邀请我们思考所有寻求更好生活之人的基本人性。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Firefighters battle wildfire tearing through Belgian nature reserve
title.zh: 消防员奋力扑灭席卷比利时自然保护区的野火

summary.en: Firefighters are battling a major wildfire in a Belgian nature reserve, described as the country's most severe in recent years.
summary.zh: 消防员正在比利时一处自然保护区扑灭一场大规模野火，这场火灾被描述为该国近年来最严重的一次。

body.en:
Firefighters battled a wildfire tearing through Belgium's largest nature reserve on Saturday, with the blaze described as the country's worst in recent history.

Residents were ordered to evacuate two nearby villages as the flames consumed a third of the High Fens, with local officials warning the fire - which had been burning since Friday - could reach homes.

Water-bombing aircraft and helicopters were sent from across Europe to aid the firefighters working in the park near its eastern border with Germany.

It was among a number of wildfires burning across Europe on Saturday, including a forest fire which caused hundreds of residents to leave their home in south-western France.

Local officials in Belgium said the blaze remained out of control as of Saturday afternoon.

Nicolas Yernaux, a spokesperson for the regional authorities in Wallonia, said the fire was the country's "largest in recent history".

"There is a risk that the fire could reach homes, but we are deploying all available resources to protect them," he said, with a nearby gymnasium opened to accommodate those evacuating their homes.

Authorities said they had been hampered by weather conditions as well as the park's terrain - which consists of bog-like territory, moorland and forests.

Firefighters had "allowed parts of the heathland to burn because the area is very difficult to access," Yernaux said.

Gregory Melotte, one of those working to extinguish the blaze, told Belgian broadcaster RTBF: "We managed to calm the fire coming from the plain, to prevent it from spreading into the fir forest. We still succeeded in our mission, but it's not over yet.

"The flames are coming towards us, the wind has shifted twice, once in our favour, once against us."

The country activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism to trigger reinforcements from other countries.

European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib said two Swedish water-bombing aircraft and two helicopters, one from the Czech Republic and one from the Netherlands, were on their way.

Meanwhile, local officials said 650 residents evacuated their homes as a wildfire burned in Landes, south-western France.

The fire began on Thursday and, according to authorities, reignited on Saturday - with more than 500 firefighters deployed to tackle the blaze.

Forest fires have also been reported in Croatia, Spain and Serbia since Friday, after a summer of extreme heat which has seen swathes of land across Europe either going up in flames or scorched brown .

The EU's climate monitoring service, Copernicus, has confirmed that western Europe experienced its hottest June-to-July period on record.
body.zh: 周六，消防队员与一场席卷比利时最大自然保护区的野火搏斗，这场大火被描述为该国近年来最严重的火灾。 由于大火吞噬了高沼泽三分之一的面积，居民被命令疏散附近的两个村庄，当地官员警告说，自周五以来一直在燃烧的大火可能会蔓延到各家各户。 欧洲各地派出水弹轰炸机和直升机，协助在靠近德国东部边境的公园工作的消防队员。 这是周六欧洲各地发生的多起野火之一，其中包括导致数百名居民离开法国西南部家园的森林火灾。 比利时当地官员表示，截至周六下午，大火仍处于失控状态。 瓦隆地区当局发言人尼古拉斯·耶诺(Nicolas Yernaux)表示，此次火灾是该国“近代历史上最大的火灾”。 他说：“火势有可能蔓延到房屋，但我们正在部署所有可用资源来保护他们。”附近的一个体育馆已开放，以容纳那些撤离家园的人。 当局表示，他们的行动受到了天气条件以及公园地形的阻碍——公园地形由沼泽地、沼泽地和森林组成。 耶诺说，消防队员“允许部分石南荒地燃烧，因为该地区很难进入”。 格雷戈里·梅洛特（Gregory Melotte）是参与灭火工作的人员之一，他告诉比利时广播公司 RTBF：“我们设法平息了来自平原的火势，防止火势蔓延到冷杉树林。我们仍然成功地完成了任务，但事情还没有结束。” “火焰正向我们袭来，风向已经改变了两次，一次对我们有利，一次对我们不利。” 该国启动了欧盟的公民保护机制，以引发其他国家的增援。 欧盟委员哈贾·拉赫比卜表示，两架瑞典水轰炸机和两架直升机（一架来自捷克共和国，一架来自荷兰）正在途中。 与此同时，当地官员表示，法国西南部朗德省发生野火，650 名居民撤离家园。 据当局称，大火于周四开始，并于周六重新燃起，并部署了 500 多名消防员来扑灭大火。 自周五以来，克罗地亚、西班牙和塞尔维亚也报告发生森林火灾，经历了一个夏季的酷热，欧洲大片土地要么着火，要么变成焦褐色。 欧盟气候监测服务机构哥白尼证实，西欧经历了有记录以来最热的六月至七月时期。

reflection.en: The devastating wildfire in Belgium reminds us of the fragility of our natural world and the profound impact of such events. Romans 8:22 speaks of creation groaning, a poignant image for the suffering ecosystems endure. As we witness these tragedies, we are called to reflect on our role in caring for the earth Yahweh has entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 比利时发生的这场毁灭性野火提醒我们自然世界的脆弱性以及此类事件的深远影响。《罗马书》8:22 提到受造之物一同叹息，这是对生态系统所承受痛苦的深刻写照。当我们目睹这些悲剧时，我们被呼召反思自己在看护雅伟托付给我们的地球方面的责任。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Multiple suspects at large after five shot at Virginia State University, police say
title.zh: 弗吉尼亚州立大学枪击案致五人受伤，一人危重

summary.en: Officials reported that five individuals were injured, one critically, during a shooting incident at Virginia State University in the early hours of Saturday. Multiple suspects were involved, according to the university.
summary.zh: 据校方称，周六凌晨，弗吉尼亚州立大学发生枪击事件，造成五人受伤，其中一人伤势严重。多名嫌疑人涉案。

body.en:
Five people have been injured, one critically, in a shooting at Virginia State University which involved multiple suspects.

Officers responded to the incident outside a residence halls at about 01:28 local time (05:28 GMT) on Saturday, the university said.

Five individuals, who were all found with gunshot wounds, were taken to local hospitals. Four had injuries which were not deemed to be life-threatening, according to the university.

Local police told the BBC on Saturday afternoon they believe more than one shooter was involved but no arrests have been made.

A temporary lockdown on the campus has since been lifted but a "significant" law enforcement presence is still on site, the university confirmed in a statement.

It added that Chesterfield County Police are leading the investigation with help from other local law enforcement and campus police.

According to the university's website, classes for the new term were set to begin on Monday and campus dormitories opened for returning students on Friday.

Lieutenant James R Lamb of Chesterfield County Police Department told the BBC one of the victims is a student and another is under 18.

"We don't have anybody in custody," Lamb said. "We know there was more than one shooter, so I would say the suspects are still at large."

He said investigators were still reviewing surveillance video for evidence and are not currently treating any of the five people who were injured as suspects.

Virginia State University (VSU) has about 5,000 students and is just over 20 miles south of Richmond, the capital of the US state of Virginia.

Such institutions were created to provide higher education to disenfranchised African Americans, who were otherwise prohibited from attending most colleges.
body.zh: 弗吉尼亚州立大学表示，该大学发生枪击事件，造成 5 人受伤，其中一人伤势严重，涉及多名嫌疑人。 周六当地时间 01:28 左右（格林威治标准时间 05:28），警方对宿舍外的事件做出了反应。 五人均被发现受枪伤，已被送往当地医院。该大学表示，四人受伤，但没有生命危险。 目前尚不清楚是否有任何嫌疑人被捕。 BBC已联系当地警方征求意见。 该大学在一份声明中证实，校园的临时封锁已经解除，但“大量”执法人员仍在现场。 它补充说，切斯特菲尔德县警方正在其他当地执法部门和校园警察的帮助下领导调查。 弗吉尼亚州立大学 (VSU) 拥有约 5,000 名学生，位于美国弗吉尼亚州首府里士满以南 20 多英里处。 这些机构的创建是为了向被剥夺公民权的非裔美国人提供高等教育，否则他们被禁止进入大多数大学。 据该大学网站称，新学期定于周一开始，校园宿舍将于周五向返校学生开放。

reflection.en: This tragic incident at Virginia State University reminds us of the destructive power of violence and the pain it inflicts on communities. Yahweh's word warns that those who resort to weapons often find themselves caught in a cycle of harm. May we seek paths of peace and safety for all, especially within our places of learning.
reflection.zh: 弗吉尼亚州立大学发生的这起悲剧事件，提醒我们暴力具有毁灭性的力量，并给社区带来痛苦。雅伟的话语警告我们，那些诉诸武器的人往往会陷入伤害的循环。愿我们为所有人，尤其是在我们的学习场所，寻求和平与安全的道路。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Body found in Romania believed to be missing British hiker George Smyth
title.zh: 罗马尼亚发现的尸体据信是失踪的英国徒步旅行者乔治·史密斯

summary.en: Family paid tribute to Bristol University geology student, 18, after being notified by Avon and Somerset police A body has been found in the search for an 18-year-old British man who went missing last year while hiking in Romania, UK police said. George Smyth, a geology student...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A body has been found in the search for an 18-year-old British man who went missing last year while hiking in Romania , UK police said.

George Smyth, a geology student at the University of Bristol , went missing in November.

On Saturday, Avon and Somerset police said a body found in the region of the country is believed to be that of Smyth.

His family have been informed and are being supported by a family liaison officer, the force added.

“He was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends.

“We want to thank Salvamont mountain rescue, who have worked tirelessly since November searching for George, despite very difficult and often dangerous conditions.

“They are an amazing team, and have remained in constant communication, helping us greatly throughout this awful time.”

Efforts will be made to return Smyth’s body to the UK once formal identification has taken place.

The family’s statement added: “We would also like to thank Avon and Somerset police and University of Bristol, who have gone above and beyond to try and find George, and to support us as a family.

“Although this latest news is incredibly painful, the torture of waiting is finally over, so we can now focus on bringing George home and saying goodbye.

“We would appreciate privacy while we continue to come to terms with this loss.”

On Wednesday, mountain rescue teams said they had resumed their search in “previously indicated areas, under rock walls, in grates and in the hard-to-reach sectors” but without success.

The student, from Newport in Shropshire, is believed to have left Poiana Brașov heading to Bran. He reached Țigănești, where he made an emergency call for help.

At the time, rescuers said he was in a “very isolated and hard to access mountain area” and the weather conditions were extremely severe with strong winds, heavy snowfall and dense fog.

The search and rescue operation also involved a canine unit, drones and helicopters being deployed.

Sebastian Marinescu, from the area’s mountain rescue service, previously told the BBC the 18-year-old “was disoriented, physically exhausted, and already showing signs of hypothermia” when they received the emergency call.
body.zh: 英国警方称，在搜寻一名去年在罗马尼亚徒步旅行时失踪的 18 岁英国男子时，发现了一具尸体。 布里斯托大学地质系学生乔治·史密斯 (George Smyth) 去年 11 月失踪。 周六，埃文和萨默塞特警方表示，在该国地区发现的一具尸体据信是史密斯的尸体。 警方补充说，他的家人已收到通知，并得到家庭联络官的支持。 “他是我们当中最优秀的人，他的弟弟、家人和朋友都深深地怀念他。 “我们要感谢萨尔瓦蒙特山救援队，他们自 11 月以来一直在不知疲倦地寻找乔治，尽管条件非常困难且往往很危险。 “他们是一支了不起的团队，一直保持着持续的沟通，在这段艰难的时期为我们提供了巨大的帮助。” 一旦正式确认身份，将努力将史密斯的遗体运回英国。 乔治一家的声明补充道：“我们还要感谢埃文和萨默塞特警方以及布里斯托尔大学，他们竭尽全力寻找乔治，并支持我们一家人。 “虽然这个最新消息令人难以置信的痛苦，但等待的折磨终于结束了，所以我们现在可以专注于带乔治回家并告别。 “在我们继续接受这种损失的同时，我们希望能够保护隐私。” 周三，山地救援队表示，他们已在“先前指定的区域、岩壁下、格栅内和难以到达的区域”恢复搜索，但没有成功。 据信，这名来自什罗普郡纽波特的学生已离开波亚娜·布拉索夫前往布兰。他到达希根什蒂并紧急拨打求救电话。 当时，救援人员表示，他身处“非常偏僻、难以进入的山区”，天气条件极其恶劣，有强风、大雪和浓雾。 搜救行动还部署了警犬队、无人机和直升机。 该地区山地救援部门的塞巴斯蒂安·马里内斯库 (Sebastian Marinescu) 此前告诉 BBC，当他们接到紧急电话时，这名 18 岁的男子“神志不清、身体疲惫，并且已经出现体温过低的迹象”。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to wisdom, knowledge, and the pursuit of truth. Proverbs 2:6 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with humble learning and wise application, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到智慧、知识与追求真理。Proverbs 2:6提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以谦卑学习与智慧运用来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, authorities say
title.zh: 当局称以色列对黎巴嫩南部发动袭击，造成11人死亡

summary.en: Israel's military conducted strikes in southern Lebanon, stating they targeted "Hezbollah terror infrastructure." This action was described as a response to earlier attacks against Israeli soldiers, resulting in eleven reported deaths.
summary.zh: 以色列军方表示，对黎巴嫩南部发动了袭击，目标是“真主党恐怖基础设施”。此次行动是以色列对早前其士兵遭受袭击的回应，据报道造成11人死亡。

body.en:
Eleven people have been killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, authorities say, in one of the deadliest days of attacks since an agreement aimed at reducing hostilities was announced in June.

Lebanon's prime minister said seven people were killed in a strike on a house on the outskirts of Ansar, 70km (43 miles) south of the capital, Beirut. State media reported three children and two women were among the dead.

Israel's Defense Forces (IDF) said it had killed a commander of Hezbollah - the Iran-backed Shia militia - following an attack against Israeli soldiers.

The commander's family "who he used as human shields" were present and "harmed", it added.

Later on Saturday, another round of strikes hit the town of Deir al-Zahrani, killing four and wounding five others, the Lebanese ministry of health said.

Lebanese authorities say the strike in Ansar at around 04:30 (01:30 GMT) occurred where displaced families were living. Footage on social media shows large plumes of smoke permeating through the streets of the village as sirens ring out.

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned the attacks, saying the seven civilians killed were not "military infrastructure".

"Israel must halt this escalation," he said. "For the security of our people and their right to life on their land are not subject to negotiation or bargaining."

The IDF said the incident that prompted its strike on Ansar had taken place in the Ali al-Taher Ridge, a strategic high ground overlooking much of south-eastern Lebanon and one of the war's most fiercely contested positions.

A later IDF statement said Ali Samir al-Haj Hassan, who it described as a Hezbollah battalion commander in the Radwan Force unit, had been killed.

"Alongside him, several additional terrorists who were involved in advancing terror attacks against IDF soldiers were eliminated," it added.

"The strike was specifically directed at Hassan, who was a lawful target under international law, not at his family members who he used as human shields - hiding alongside them inside the military HQ," the IDF said.

Lebanon was drawn into the war between Israel, the US and Iran on 2 March, when Hezbollah - the armed group affiliated with Iran - launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for a strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

Israel responded by launching a bombing campaign across Lebanon and invading a significant part of the country's south. Its forces continue to occupy roughly 5% of Lebanese territory.

The June ceasefire framework calls for Hezbollah to disarm, Israeli forces to withdraw gradually from southern Lebanon and the Lebanese army to deploy across the area.

summary.en: Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

body.en:
Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

At least 11 people were killed when Israel launched fresh airstrikes in southern Lebanon  on Saturday, the deadliest since the Israel-Hezbollah truce nearly two months ago.

The attacks were met with defiance by the Iran-backed Hezbollah , which demanded an end to "humiliating" peace negotiations with Israel .

The Lebanese Health Ministry said one of the strikes, on the edge of the village of Ansar, killed seven people and wounded two.

The strike, which happened at dawn, hit a house and destroyed it, according to NNA, the Lebanese state news agency.

Germany's DPA news agency cited residents as saying the property served as a base for Hezbollah.

The second strike hit the village of Deir al-Zahrani, killing four and wounding 17.

NNA reported other strikes around the strategic Ali Taher hill, which overlooks parts of the southern city of Nabatiyeh and key roads to it.

The Israeli military confirmed hitting Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, saying it was retaliation for an attack by the militia on Israeli forces.

Later Saturday, Hezbollah hit back at the latest strikes, saying they would be met with an "appropriate" response.

Israel "must clearly understand that its attacks, violations and attempts to impose a fait accompli cannot continue, and will be met with an appropriate response", the Iran-backed group said in a statement.

Hezbollah warned Lebanese authorities against continuing its "humiliating" negotiations with Israel, which would provide "the enemy with free concessions."

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced the strikes, calling on Israel to "halt this escalation."

"The seven martyrs of the Israeli airstrike on the town of Ansar are not military infrastructure and the children and women killed were not military targets,” he wrote on X.

The Israel–Hezbollah war reignited in early March around the start of the  Iran war , when Hezbollah launched attacks on northern Israel to avenge the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

It rapidly became a full-scale conflict that involved Israeli ground operations in southern Lebanon, mass evacuations of residents and the deaths of over 4,300 people.

Israel claims to have established the so-called security zone in southern Lebanon to prevent Hezbollah attacks on northern Israel. 

According to Lebanese media, the Israeli-controlled area covers approximately 620 square kilometres, or about 6% of the country's total area.

summary.en: South Korea's opposition leader, Lee Jae Myung, has proposed talks to officially end the Korean War, which has been in a frozen state since an armistice was signed in 1953.

body.en:
South Korea's president has proposed talks with its northern neighbour on officially ending the war between the two that is technically still active.

Lee Jae Myung suggested a "multi-layered security system" to avoid flare-ups along the countries' de-facto border, known as the demilitarised zone (DMZ), and offered to discuss practical ways of halting Pyongyang's nuclear ambitions.

North Korea has continually tested ballistic missiles capable of carrying nuclear warheads, which has been perceived in Seoul and nearby Japan as an attempt to intimidate and project power.

The conflict between the two occupants of the Korean peninsula has been effectively frozen since an armistice was signed in 1953.

They did not sign a peace treaty and therefore have remained technically still at war ever since.

There have been clashes and tensions along the DMZ in the decades since, along with accusations from both sides of provocations, including dropping balloons carrying rubbish and propaganda .

Lee, who became South Korean president last year after his predecessor Yoon Suk Yeol was impeached for attempting to declare martial law, has sought to thaw relations with North Korea and its ally China, which had soured under Yoon.

"Let us put down our intentions to threaten each other and begin discussions to end the long-running war as the directly involved parties," he told a ceremony marking Liberation Day, which commemorates the peninsula's liberation from Japanese rule.

Lee expressed hope that the two nations "will sit face-to-face for peaceful coexistence and mutual growth", adding this could serve as a forum for discussing "effective ways to halt the advancement of the North's nuclear capabilities".

North Korea has yet to react to Lee's offer. The authoritarian regime's state news agency carried news of Kim marking the country's own Liberation Day commemorations with a wreath-laying and guard of honour.

Pyongyang has previously rebuffed Lee's offers of engagement, criticising a deal for the US to build South Korea a fleet of nuclear-powered submarines and denouncing joint drills between the two allies.

In January 2024, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un announced that unification with the South was no longer possible.

Kim said that the constitution should be amended to educate North Koreans that South Korea was a "primary foe and invariable principal enemy".

In a speech at the time, he added that if a war were to break out on the Korean peninsula, the North should aim towards "occupying", "recapturing" and "incorporating" the South into its territory.

title.en: Russians snap up new homes built on Ukraine 'graveyard'

summary.en: Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?

Halyna Artemova, an English teacher, lived in Mariupol for almost 40 years, at Metallurgy Avenue 87.

"It's my beloved city. When I look at the photos, it brings tears to my eyes. I know every crack in the asphalt, every tree," she told DW. Her apartment block in the city on the Sea of Azov was struck by a missile during a Russian attack in March 2022.

Photographer Yevhen Sosnovsky and his wife lived in the house next door, Metallurgy Avenue 85, for 20 years. "I did everything myself, all the interior renovations, and the furniture," he said. "We invested a lot in it; we planned to spend our twilight years there, living quietly." His building also caught fire during the missile attack, and residents were driven out by Russian troops. They weren't even allowed to take food or clothing with them.

Now there's a parking lot where Sosnovsky's apartment block used to be. Next door, where Artemova once lived, stands a new building. The Russian building contractor Su-2007, which operates in the Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, cleared several buildings on Metallurgy Avenue that were destroyed in the war and constructed high-rise apartment blocks in their place. These form part of a residential complex now known as the Leningradsky Kvartal.

"They're building on human bones, and fast, to eradicate the traces of their crimes," said Sosnovsky.

DW is not allowed in to the Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine, so cannot report directly from city. However, it is possible to get an idea of what life is like in Mariupol today by talking to people who used to live there, studying satellite images, and doing research online.

Many people who have moved into the new apartments on Metallurgy Avenue communicate with each other online in neighborhood forums. From these forums, it's clear that the majority bought the apartments either to live in themselves, or to rent out.

In chats, they ask how they can get furniture delivered from Russia, or which kindergarten or school they should choose for their children. People are reminded that the most important thing when submitting documents is that they should be of Russian origin.

Not everyone has finished remodeling their apartments, and some people with small children take the opportunity to complain: "It's too late! Stop the goddamn renovations! Or maybe you're pro-Ukrainian and oppose Russian laws?"

Economist Vyacheslav Shiryaev said apartments in the new buildings in Mariupol are being bought primarily by incomers: Russian security personnel, officials and people working in military...
body.zh: 俄罗斯正在被占领的乌克兰城市马里乌波尔的废墟上建造高层建筑。谁在购买这些房产？曾经住在这里的乌克兰人怎么样了？ Halyna Artemova 是一名英语教师，她在马里乌波尔冶金大道 87 号居住了近 40 年。 “这是我深爱的城市。当我看到这些照片时，我热泪盈眶。我熟悉沥青路上的每一条裂缝，每一棵树，”她告诉德国之声。她位于亚速海城市的公寓楼在 2022 年 3 月的俄罗斯袭击中被导弹击中。 摄影师叶夫亨·索斯诺夫斯基 (Yevhen Sosnovsky) 和他的妻子在隔壁冶金大道 85 号的房子里住了 20 年。 “所有的事情都是我自己做的，所有的室内装修和家具，”他说。 “我们投入了很多，打算在那里安度晚年，安静地生活。”他的大楼也在导弹袭击中起火，居民被俄罗斯军队赶出。他们甚至不被允许携带食物或衣服。 现在索斯诺夫斯基的公寓楼原来是一个停车场。隔壁是阿尔特莫娃曾经居住过的地方，矗立着一座新建筑。在被俄罗斯占领的乌克兰地区开展业务的俄罗斯建筑承包商Su-2007清除了冶金大道上几座在战争中被摧毁的建筑物，并在其所在地建造了高层公寓楼。这些是现在称为列宁格勒克瓦尔塔尔的住宅区的一部分。 索斯诺夫斯基说：“他们正在人骨上快速建造，以消除他们的犯罪痕迹。” 德国之声不允许进入俄罗斯占领的乌克兰地区，因此无法直接从城市报道。然而，通过与曾经住在那里的人交谈、研究卫星图像和在线研究，可以了解马里乌波尔今天的生活。 许多搬进冶金大道新公寓的人都在社区论坛上在线交流。从这些论坛可以明显看出，大多数人购买公寓要么是为了自己居住，要么是为了出租。 在聊天中，他们询问如何从俄罗斯获得家具，或者应该为孩子选择哪家幼儿园或学校。 人们被提醒，提交文件时最重要的是它们应该是俄罗斯裔。 并不是每个人都完成了他们的公寓的改造，一些带着小孩的人趁机抱怨：“太晚了！停止该死的装修！或者也许你是亲乌克兰的，反对俄罗斯法律的？” 经济学家维亚切斯拉夫·希里亚耶夫 (Vyacheslav Shiryaev) 表示，马里乌波尔新建筑中的公寓主要由外来者购买：俄罗斯安全人员、官员和军队工作人员……

body.en:
While ongoing military actions in Gaza and settler attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have largely isolated Israel globally, Latin America's authoritarian right sees an opening for a strategic alliance.

A three-week military offensive in the Gaza Strip  in 2009, which killed more than 1,400 people, including an estimated 1,100 civilians, spurred Venezuela's Socialist president at the time, Hugo Chavez, to expel the Israeli ambassador in protest and end diplomatic relations.

Seventeen years later, Venezuela and Israel have agreed to establish a mechanism for the resumption of consular services. It's a limited step, but one that until recently would have been unthinkable.

In Colombia , the nationalist government of new President Abelardo de la Espriella recently reversed the decision by his predecessor, Gustavo Petro , to sever diplomatic relations with Israel in protest of the country's most recent war in Gaza , which has killed more than 70,000 people, nearly one-third of them children.

De la Espriella has even announced that Colombia will relocate its embassy to Jerusalem, and this week declared that Colombia would join the United States as the only two countries that recognize "Israeli sovereignty" over the Golan Heights, which is Syrian territory under international law but has been occupied by Israel since 1967. The vast majority of the international community, including Germany and the UN, does not recognize the annexation of the Golan Heights by Israel.

"There is a trend toward rapprochement with Israel as a response to the surge of the radical right in the region," said Isaac Caro, a professor at Alberto Hurtado University in Chile. Caro said authoritarians in Latin America were linking relations with Israel to "an active alignment with US foreign policy ." He said reinforcing ties with Israel had become a characteristic of Latin America's radical right as part of the renewed discourse of region's place in Judeo-Christian Western civilization.

In Argentina, for example, ultraconservative President Javier Milei has made close relations with Israel a defining feature of both his foreign policy and his own political identity.

Daniel Wajner, associate professor of international relations at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, said there had been a "surge" in diplomacy between Israel and Latin American governments. Wajner said Jair Bolsonaro , the neoliberal former president of Brazil, and El Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, the self-described "world's coolest dictator," were early adopters of warmer ties with Israel. They were followed by Milei and others.

The United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi National Oil ‌Company said two of its vessels were attacked transiting the strait on Thursday evening. The UAE government blamed Iran, which made no immediate comment.

summary.en: At least 38 people have been killed after a major earthquake hit Indonesia, sparking fears of a destructive tsunami earlier on Saturday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least 38 people have died after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday, which was followed by dozens of aftershocks.

"Thirty-eight people have been confirmed dead, two were seriously injured, 11 sustained minor injuries, and approximately 2,000 people have evacuated on their own," Indonesian National Disaster Mitigation Agency chief Suharyanto told a news conference on Saturday.

The earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia early Saturday, sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning.

Tsunami waves of less than one metre were recorded in several areas of the Southeast Asian nation. The warning was later lifted.

Residents in Nagekeo regency on Flores, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated.

Teams had yet to reach Nagekeo, and communications signals there had been ‌affected, Fathur Rahman, head of the city's rescue agency, told Reuters.

Attempts to reach Nagekeo ⁠by car were blocked by landslides, while another team was attempting to go by ferry, he said.

About 2,000 residents in Nagekeo evacuated, and damage was reported to a number of houses, warehouses and government facilities, national disaster mitigation agency BNPB said.

Authorities also reported traffic congestion and power outages affecting parts of the regency, it said.

The governor of East Nusa Tenggara Province, Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena, told a media conference at least five people died from collapsing rubble as they slept.

The epicentre of the shallow quake was located off the north coast of the island, about 68 kilometres northwest of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said.

The initial jolt was followed by strong aftershocks in the same area, including one with a magnitude of 6.1.

"Suddenly it started to shake and I panicked," 31-year-old hospital customer service official and Maumere resident, Lukas Lotar, told AFP.

"Patients also fled the hospital, the jolt was big. I saw some walls were cracked," he said.

A resident in Nagekeo, Yohanes Babo, 56, said he was at a market when the earth started shaking.

"The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house," he told AFP.

"People were panicking, running here and there. We're evacuating for the time being... and trying to get to the hills," he said, adding: "My family is safe. No one was harmed."

Strong shaking was also felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara and parts of South Sulawesi, and residents in several areas reported shaking lasting about one minute, BNPB said in a statement.

title.en: Five years on from the fall of Kabul: Taliban celebrate while Australia laments
title.zh: 喀布尔陷落五年后：塔利班庆祝，澳大利亚哀叹

summary.en: Amid fresh UN detentions and new legal actions, Australia joins global pressure on Kabul's deepening isolation.

body.en:
The Taliban government has marked five years since returning to power in Afghanistan, celebrating its rule with public events and military displays.

Meanwhile, Australia, the United Nations, and human rights groups highlight a deepening humanitarian crisis and systematic repression of women.

In Kabul, white flags of the Islamic Emirate adorned streets alongside decorated US military vehicles left behind during the chaotic 2021 withdrawal.

Taliban authorities hosted sports matches — from which women are barred — to commemorate their takeover, asserting that independence has brought national security and economic stability.

Taliban government chief spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said authorities were laying the "foundations of the economy" and appealed for patience.

However, World Bank data shows declining per capita GDP, exacerbated by the return of over six million Afghans from Iran and Pakistan over the past three years.

In a joint statement on Saturday, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles, Foreign Minister Penny Wong, and Immigration Minister Tony Burke acknowledged the milestone while reaffirming Australia's commitment to holding the Taliban accountable.

"Five years on from the fall of Kabul, our thoughts are with the people of Afghanistan, who continue to face violent repression at the hands of the Taliban, as well as the Afghan community in Australia and around the world," the statement read.

The government leaders honored the service of more than 39,000 Australian Defence Force and civilian personnel who served in Afghanistan over two decades, remembering the 41 soldiers who died during operations and those lost after returning home.

The statement noted that Australia has provided $310 million in direct aid through non-government channels since September 2021, while establishing an autonomous sanctions framework against senior Taliban figures and backing international action under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW).

"Australia has not stepped back from that responsibility," ministers stated, pointing to expanded migration pathways for displaced Afghans and ongoing support for locally engaged Afghan employees now living in Australia.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) reported this week that six male employees of an Afghan legal rights NGO were forcibly disappeared in Kabul, while Taliban intelligence officers in Herat detained two UN Assistance Mission (UNAMA) staff members.

title.en: 'I've never seen scenes like this': Why Britain is burning
title.zh: “我从未见过这样的场景”：为什么英国在燃烧

summary.en: Prime Minister Andy Burnham urges a clean energy transition as wildfires gut homes and leave Britain a "tinderbox".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Friday that Britain must face up to the reality of the changing climate and accelerate its move to clean energy as he visited a town gutted by wildfire.

In Stourbridge, near the UK's second-largest city of Birmingham, smoke rose from smouldering ruins of several roofless houses as firefighters sprayed water on the wreckage.

The West Midlands Fire Service said 19 houses were completely destroyed and 18 others damaged in the town.

Meeting firefighters there after viewing the scene, Burnham said the "combustible situation" was related to climate change and showed the need for a more rapid clean energy transition.

"I've never seen scenes like this in Britain, where you just see a whole house gutted, smouldering," he said.

"We have to face up to the changing climate ... there's no point denying where we are. We need to face up to it. We need more clean energy."

Burnham — who took power last month — has faced criticism for not directly referencing climate change sooner, as Britain, like much of Europe, has grappled for weeks with widespread drought, extreme heat, and wildfires.

The UK has set a target to consume zero carbon-based electricity by 2030 and is aiming to reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 to combat climate change.

Describing Britain as "a tinderbox" with 37 blazes nationwide on Friday, the prime minister warned against lighting fires outdoors, as the government introduced a ban on selling disposable barbecue equipment.

People across England and Wales began receiving a rare emergency alert on their phones from 7:00pm local time, warning them not to light "anything that could spark a fire, including barbecues, campfires, and fireworks".

Residents of Stourbridge were evacuated, and some were treated for smoke inhalation after the fire there spread on Thursday, the UK's hottest day of the year so far. Temperatures reached a high of 38.1C in west London.

One firefighter was hospitalised and five others suffered minor injuries, the fire service confirmed, with crews continuing to extinguish "hotspots" in open grassland, along a railway and in gardens.

Six other firefighters farther north in Staffordshire were taken to hospital suffering from smoke inhalation and heat exhaustion battling similar blazes there, the fire service said.

The ambulance service in the West Midlands region, including Stourbridge and Staffordshire, said it had treated 68 people Thursday with symptoms such as smoke inhalation, 25 of whom were hospitalised.

title.en: Donald Trump to declare Hormuz US territory 'soon'
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普“很快”宣布霍尔木兹为美国领土

summary.en: Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.

President Donald Trump said Friday that he would "soon" declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory.

"After we finish defeating Iran , which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States," Trump said at a rally at a police academy in Garden City, New York state. "It's true," he added.

It was not clear whether his remarks were serious or whether they signal a new policy shift for Washington in its war against Tehran , which is more than five months old.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi dismissed Trump's remarks, saying the country would "not be intimidated" and that the strategic waterway would remain under its control and authority.

The US and Israel launched the war against Iran on February 28. At the time, senior White House officials, including Trump, said the aim was to end Iran's nuclear program and spark a popular uprising to force regime change in the Islamic Republic, among other goals.

Iran's response has been to target US allies across the Middle East with drone and missile strikes, as well as to impose a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments passed before the war.

The US responded to Iran's closure of the strait with its own naval blockade of Iranian ships and ports. The two countries have been locked in a stalemate over the vital waterway for months, causing energy prices to soar.

Rising oil and gas costs and the economic fallout from the war are likely to be leading issues in the midterm elections in November.

During the rally, the US president also urged Americans to accept that they would have to "pay a tiny little bit more" for their gasoline as a worthy price for preventing "a very evil country" from getting a nuclear weapon.

"What we're doing is a great service for the world, not only for ourselves ... and we're really doing a ​great job," Trump told the crowd, adding that "no ships get through (the US blockade of Hormuz) unless we want them to."

On Friday, Trump also dismissed concerns over the living conditions aboard a US aircraft carrier that was deployed to the Middle East amid the war with Iran.

Relatives of service members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln told US military media outlets that personnel are struggling with difficult living conditions and deteriorating mental health . There have also been reports of suicide attempts.

body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，伊朗被击败后，该海峡将成为美国的一部分。他还告诉美国人接受更高的天然气价格，自从伊朗因美国和以色列的袭击而关闭霍尔木兹海峡以来，天然气价格已经飙升。 唐纳德·特朗普总统周五表示，他将“很快”宣布霍尔木兹海峡为美国领土。 特朗普在纽约州花园城一所警察学院的集会上说：“在我们击败伊朗之后，伊朗正在被击败，很快我就会宣布霍尔木兹海峡是美国的领土。” “这是真的，”他补充道。 目前尚不清楚他的言论是否严肃，或者是否标志着华盛顿在对德黑兰的战争中发生了新的政策转变，这场战争已经持续了五个多月。 伊朗副外长卡泽姆·加里巴迪驳斥了特朗普的言论，称该国“不会被吓倒”，战略航道将继续处于其控制和管辖之下。 美国和以色列于 2 月 28 日对伊朗发动战争。当时，包括特朗普在内的白宫高级官员表示，其目标包括结束伊朗核计划并引发民众起义，迫使伊朗伊斯兰共和国政权更迭。 伊朗的回应是用无人机和导弹袭击美国在中东的盟友，并封锁霍尔木兹海峡，战前世界上五分之一的石油和液化天然气（LNG）运输均通过霍尔木兹海峡。 美国对伊朗关闭海峡的回应是对伊朗船只和港口进行海上封锁。几个月来，两国在这条重要水道问题上陷入僵局，导致能源价格飙升。 石油和天然气成本上涨以及战争造成的经济影响可能成为 11 月中期选举的主要问题。 在集会期间，美国总统还敦促美国人接受这一事实：他们必须为汽油“多付一点钱”，作为防止“一个非常邪恶的国家”获得核武器的合理代价。 特朗普对人群说：“我们正在做的事情是为世界提供伟大的服务，不仅是为了我们自己……而且我们确实做得很好。”他补充说，“除非我们希望，否则没有船只可以通过（美国对霍尔木兹的封锁）。” 周五，特朗普还驳回了对在与伊朗战争期间部署到中东的一艘美国航空母舰上生活条件的担忧。 亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰上服役人员的亲属告诉美国军方媒体，人员正在与艰苦的生活条件和不断恶化的心理健康作斗争。 也有自杀未遂的报道。 特朗普否认这艘已经在海上航行了九个月的航母的部署...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: China Desk
title.zh: 中国观察

strap.en: Policy signals, social change, and national developments inside China.
strap.zh: 聚焦中国内部政策走向、社会变化与国家动态。

title.en: How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing
title.zh: 如何购买“巨型橡皮艇”：穿越英吉利海峡的危险新模式

summary.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. Additional reporting by Lyndon Li Continue reading...
body.zh: 载有数百人的船只是一个明显且令人震惊的趋势。但这么大的船只从哪里来呢？他们表示，只要订单超过 20 艘，提供一艘在西欧波涛汹涌的海域使用的大型小艇就不成问题。这家中国公司的销售经理甚至还为一位冒充潜在客户的卫报卧底记者准备了一份在线手册供其细读。他们的生产能力为每月 500 艘船，是的，有可能以合适的价格获得更大的船。他们可以以每艘 1,678 美元（1,238 英镑）的价格制造一艘七米甚至八米长的军用小艇，不带发动机，但这将缺乏 CE 认证，这是表明产品符合欧盟健康和安全要求的强制性标志。林登·李的补充报道继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: The Fauci hearing was painful to watch. But we need answers on Covid-19’s origin| David Relman
title.zh: 福奇的听证会看起来很痛苦。但我们需要 Covid-19 起源的答案|大卫雷尔曼

summary.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. David Relman is a professor of medicine and microbiology at Stanford University. He was an inaugural member of the US National Science Advisory Board for Biosecurity and president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管最近在国会举行了听证会，但我们似乎距离了解 Covid-19 起源的目标比以往任何时候都更远。作为一名微生物学家和传染病临床医生，很难看到最近公众关于 Covid-19 起源的讨论的转移。对我来说，阅读安东尼·福奇在他现已公开的日记中关于起源争论的评论尤其困难。 7 月 29 日美国参议员兰德·保罗主持的电视节目对福奇进行敌意审讯，令人感到痛苦。尽管包括我自己在内的许多人早期呼吁对我们所知道、不知道和需要了解的 Covid-19 起源进行冷静、客观的评估，但我们现在似乎比以往任何时候都离这个目标更远——受到政治化、两极分化和不合逻辑思维的困扰。大卫·雷尔曼是斯坦福大学医学和微生物学教授。他是美国国家生物安全科学咨询委员会的首任成员和美国传染病学会主席继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到领导、智慧与公共责任。Proverbs 11:14提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以智慧、正直与服事来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: ‘TikTok wouldn’t open at all’: Taiwan simulates an internet blackout, with an eye on China threat
title.zh: “抖音完全打不开”：台湾模拟互联网中断，以应对中国威胁

summary.en: Taiwan conducted its first internet blackout simulation, prompted by concerns over the security of its undersea cables, which are vital for its digital connectivity. During the exercise in Taipei, air raid sirens sounded, mobile alerts pinged, and police directed people off the streets.
summary.zh: 台湾周四首次进行互联网中断模拟演习，原因是担心作为其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全。在台北的演习中，防空警报响起，手机警报提示音不断，警察引导人们离开街道。

body.en: Taiwan practised cutting off internet for the first time amid concerns about the safety of the undersea cables that form its ‘digital lifeline’ In Taipei, the streets swiftly empty as air raid sirens ring out and alerts ping on mobile phones. Police officers usher any stragglers into shelters, leaving the capital suddenly deserted. In cities across Taiwan, these kinds of drills are a fact of life every year , amid the growing threat posed by China across the strait, but this time there is something different. Continue reading...
body.zh: 由于担心构成其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全性，台湾周四首次练习切断互联网。在台北，随着空袭警报的响起和手机上的警报声，街道迅速空无一人。警察把掉队的人带进避难所，首都突然变得空无一人。在台湾各城市，随着海峡两岸中国构成的威胁日益加剧，此类演习每年都是家常便饭，但这次有所不同。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Taiwan's simulation of an internet blackout highlights the deep anxieties nations face regarding critical infrastructure and potential threats. In moments of such vulnerability and preparation, the ancient promise of Yahweh reminds us not to fear or be dismayed, for divine presence offers strength and help. This spiritual anchor can guide communities as...
reflection.zh: 台湾模拟互联网中断，凸显了各国在关键基础设施和潜在威胁面前的深层焦虑。在面对这种脆弱和准备的时刻，雅伟的古老应许提醒我们不要惧怕，也不要惊惶，因为神圣的同在提供力量和帮助。这个属灵的锚点可以指引社群应对复杂的挑战并建立韧性。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: The west turns a blind eye to Xi Jinping’s repressive regime in China | Letters
title.zh: 西方国家对习近平在中国的压制性政权视而不见 | 来信

summary.en: Jennifer Hubbard and other letter writers express concern that Western nations are ignoring China's repressive regime, particularly its 'ethnic unity' law used to suppress minorities. They argue that meaningful international diplomacy is urgently needed to address these human rights issues.
summary.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德及其他来信者表示，西方国家对中国压制性政权，特别是其用于压制少数民族的“民族团结”法视而不见。他们认为，急需有意义的国际外交来解决这些人权问题。

body.en: Meaningful diplomacy on an international level is well overdue, writes Jennifer Hubbard . Plus letters from Geoffrey Dixon and Jane Renton In his article on China’s latest tool for suppression of minorities, the “ethnic unity” law, Simon Tisdall seems to take it as read that western governments will continue to pay lip service to notions of human rights in China while pursuing short-term economic goals, ultimately destructive to their own productivity ( President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip, 8 August ). This has been the pattern since June 1989, the Tiananmen Square massacre. His faint hope that the young urban Chinese might overturn Xi’s regime is a judgment on the failure of western governments to show any foresight, integrity, effective diplomacy, joined-up thinking or action. They rely on the self-sacrifice of individuals such as Jimmy Lai , Lobga Rangzen and countless – often to us nameless – individuals who put their lives on the line while we wring our hands and weep crocodile tears. Continue reading...
body.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德写道，早就应该在国际层面开展有意义的外交。再加上杰弗里·迪克森和简·伦顿的来信。西蒙·蒂斯达尔在其关于中国镇压少数民族的最新工具“民族团结”法的文章中似乎认为，西方政府将继续对中国的人权观念口头上说好，同时追求短期经济目标，最终损害他们自己的生产力（习主席从来不会浪费一场好的危机。随着伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散了世界的注意力，他加强了控制，8月8日）。这就是1989年6月天安门广场屠杀以来的模式。他对中国城市年轻人可能推翻习近平政权的微弱希望是对西方政府未能表现出任何远见、正直、有效外交、联合思维或行动的判断。他们依赖于黎智英（Jimmy Lai）、洛布加·让赞（Lobga Rangzen）等个人的自我牺牲，以及无数（通常对我们来说无名）个人的自我牺牲，他们冒着生命危险，而我们则绞尽脑汁，流下鳄鱼的眼泪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international diplomacy to address the suppression of minorities echoes the biblical mandate to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. In a world where powerful voices can overshadow the vulnerable, Yahweh reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and the rights of the destitute. May we seek wisdom and courage to uphold...
reflection.zh: 呼吁国际外交以解决少数民族受压迫的问题，与圣经中为不能为自己说话之人发声的命令不谋而合。在一个强大声音可能掩盖弱势群体的世界里，雅伟提醒我们有责任倡导正义和维护贫困者的权利。愿我们寻求智慧和勇气，维护所有人的尊严，特别是那些声音被压制的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
title.zh: 台湾称遭受“异常”人工智能辅助网络攻击

summary.en: Taiwan reported detecting "abnormal" AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies last month, originating from overseas. These attacks represent a new kind of threat, with suspected links to China-based hackers.
summary.zh: 台湾报告称，上个月侦测到来自海外、由人工智能辅助的“异常”网络攻击，目标是政府机构。这些攻击代表了一种新型威胁，据称与中国相关黑客有关。

body.en: Taiwan’s statement comes a day after reports that suspected China-linked hackers had carried out a first-of-a-kind breach Taiwan says it detected AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies that came from overseas last month, a new kind of threat that has been reported as “first-of-a-kind breach”. The Ministry of Digital Affairs (MDA) said its cybersecurity monitoring units ‌detected the “abnormal attack” targeting government agencies, which began on 20 July. The National Institute of Cyber Security issued a series of warning alerts while it investigated. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾发表声明的前一天，有报道称疑似与中国有关的黑客实施了史无前例的违规行为。台湾表示，上个月检测到来自海外的针对政府机构的人工智能辅助网络攻击，这是一种新的威胁，被报道为“史无前例的违规行为”。数字事务部 (MDA) 表示，其网络安全监控单位检测到 7 月 20 日开始的针对政府机构的“异常攻击”。美国国家网络安全研究所在调查过程中发布了一系列警告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The emergence of AI-assisted cyber-attacks highlights the constant need for vigilance in a rapidly changing world. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that wisdom lies in foreseeing danger and taking appropriate refuge. As technology evolves, so must our discernment and protective measures, trusting Yahweh for guidance.
reflection.zh: 人工智能辅助的网络攻击的出现，凸显了在快速变化的世界中保持警惕的持续必要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取适当的避难措施。随着科技发展，我们的洞察力和保护措施也必须随之进步，信靠雅伟的指引。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: With Hollywood struggling in China, can the Odyssey draw a crowd?
title.zh: 好莱坞在中国市场举步维艰，《奥德赛》能否吸引观众？

summary.en: Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster, "The Odyssey" (likely Oppenheimer), is set for release across China's Imax screens. This comes at a time when Western films generally face difficulties in the Chinese market, and the film itself has reportedly overcome significant opposition.
summary.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》（很可能是《奥本海默》）将在中国各地的IMAX影院上映。目前西方电影在中国市场普遍举步维艰，而这部影片据报道也克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击。

body.en: Christopher Nolan’s epic will be released on Friday across most of the country’s 800 Imax screens, at a time when western films have been struggling The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster juggernaut, has overcome an onslaught of attacks from the world’s richest man and stared down criticism from a classicist who translated the poem , to become one of the year’s most celebrated and highest-grossing films. But this week, the film faces one of its biggest challenges yet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的这部史诗巨制将于周五在全国 800 块 Imax 银幕上上映，当时西方电影一直在苦苦挣扎，克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击，也顶住了翻译这首诗的古典学家的批评，成为今年最著名和票房最高的电影之一。但本周，这部电影面临着迄今为止最大的挑战之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Launching any major endeavor, like a film in a challenging market, requires immense effort and hope for success. Proverbs 16:3 reminds us to commit our work to Yahweh, trusting that He will establish our plans. Even when facing significant headwinds, we can find peace in knowing that our diligent efforts are seen and can be blessed.
reflection.zh: 在充满挑战的市场中推出一部电影这样的大型项目，需要付出巨大的努力并寄予成功的希望。箴言16:3提醒我们，要将我们的工作交托给雅伟，相信他会成就我们的计划。即使面对重重阻力，我们也能在知道自己的辛勤努力被看见并蒙福时找到平安。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Zhu Rongji obituary
title.zh: 朱镕基讣告

summary.en: Zhu Rongji, the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China, has passed away at 97. He was widely recognized as an economic reformer who famously declared China 'the factory of the world' and was regarded as one of the country's most effective administrators.
summary.zh: 中华人民共和国第五任总理朱镕基逝世，享年97岁。他被广泛认为是经济改革家，曾宣布中国成为‘世界工厂’，并被视为该国最有效的管理者之一。

body.en: Premier of the People’s Republic of China regarded as an economic reformer who declared that the country had become ‘the factory of the world’ Zhu Rongji, who has died aged 97, was the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China and one of its most effective administrators and economic reformers following its foundation in 1949. body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

title.en: Investors have backed off the housing market. But will you benefit?

summary.en: New data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics indicates an 8.6 per cent drop in investor loans during the June quarter, raising questions about the long-term presence of investors in the housing market.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚统计局的最新数据显示，6月份投资者贷款数量下降了8.6%，这引发了关于投资者是否会永久退出房地产市场的问题。

body.en:
Investors are shying away from the housing market — but experts say it might not be the win the government says it is.

New Australian Bureau of Statistics data on loans show investors have pulled back sharply from the housing market in the June quarter.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said on Friday the lending figures were an "encouraging sign" that Labor's changes to negative gearing and the capital gains discount were working as intended and the market was "shifting in favour of first-home buyers" — even before the changes have officially taken effect.

But experts said the retreat hasn't necessarily translated into the wave of first-home buyers the federal government's property tax changes were designed to generate.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The number of investor loans fell 8.6 per cent in the June quarter, while first-home buyer loans fell a comparatively lower 2.9 per cent, according to ABS data released on Friday.

Independent property researcher Cameron Kusher said ABS' latest lending data was not surprising and reflected a typical knee-jerk reaction to policy changes.

“Across both the number and the value, the biggest falls in lending over the quarter were for investors, which is not really a surprise when you consider the tax changes that have happened,” he said.

The pullback lines up with what major banks have been reporting in their own lending figures, with CBA and NAB both reporting a 15 per cent drop in mortgage applications last quarter, while Westpac saw a 20 per cent drop.

The tax changes were announced in the May budget but aren't set to formally take effect until 1 July 2027. So, this quarter's fall was a reaction to the announcement itself, not the policy in action.

"We may actually see a larger fall when we get to the next quarter, when we see the full impact of a whole quarter of these changes," he said.

Both Kusher and Real Estate Group's economist Luc Redman say investors have not retreated entirely, rather they have changed strategy.

They are still keen on residential property but the type of property they’re chasing has shifted. They are now eyeing properties that have strong rental growth, or yield.

"Early evidence post-budget suggests that investors are enquiring more towards units that tend to have a higher yield and a lower entry point … compared to prior, when investors would be looking at houses that have stronger prospects of capital growth," Redman told SBS News.

Two places, Tasmania and the ACT, didn't see drops in investor interest — which Kusher said could be a sign they're moving toward properties with good rental returns relative to purchase...

title.en: 'Broken and grateful': Alice Springs farewells Kumanjayi Little Baby
title.zh: “心碎又感激”：爱丽斯泉告别库曼贾伊小宝贝

summary.en: There was a sombre atmosphere at Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral, with speeches punctuated by the cries of mourners.

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

Alice Springs is known as the Red Centre of Australia but on 15 August, the community donned pink for the funeral of five-year-old Warlpiri girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby .

Warlpiri Elder and family spokesperson Robin Granites said pink was her favourite colour — it "reminds us of the clothes she used to wear".

"And the times when we would go in the evening, you see the sunset and even the early morning, you see the pink colour of clouds and that ... is a really good colour for us," Granites said ahead of the funeral.

Kumanjayi Little Baby's body was found on 30 April, after she went missing from Old Timers town camp, south of Alice Springs. Her disappearance sparked a five-day search, described as one of the largest search efforts in Northern Territory history.

47-year-old Jefferson Lewis has since been charged with her alleged murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons .

Pastor Rejeili Paulo-Smith spoke on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother at the funeral service.

She requested that her daughter be remembered , "for who she was, not simply for the tragedy of how her life ended".

"Kumanjayi wasn't simply a little girl who was known by the community. She was Mum's baby too. She was a little girl whose presence filled their home and whose absence has left an enormous space," Paulo-Smith said.

It's been almost four months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby. During this time, her family and Indigenous communities have engaged in the grieving period and mourning process known as Sorry Business .

In recent months, Paulo-Smith said the community had felt "both broken and grateful".

"Broken because a precious little life has been taken from us far too soon, yet grateful because Kumanjayi Little Baby was here. She was known, she was loved, she mattered," she said.

The week following Kumanjayi Little Baby's death, thousands of Australians gathered at nationwide candlelight vigils.

At a local vigil in Alice Springs, 89-year-old Maya Cifali told NITV News the outpouring of community spirit was unlike anything she had ever seen.

"It is the first time that such a community spirit is felt for all of us," Cifali said.

Granites also believes the local community has displayed the Warlpiri concept of Jintangka; "which means we're all in one, everyone together".

At the funeral, he took the opportunity to thank Australians and people overseas for rallying behind his family during and in the months following the search...

title.en: Beautiful, remote and running on diesel: The Daintree's power struggle

body.en:

In her backyard, Tamara Scenna takes a deep breath beneath the towering canopy of the Daintree Rainforest in Far North Queensland.

Streams of light filter through layers of ferns and fan palms as she pauses beside a running stream.

Birds sing in an off-beat chorus, providing a tranquil soundtrack to one of the oldest rainforests.

It's the perfect setting for forest bathing — a Japanese practice of immersing oneself in nature.

"I think it's about seeing the forest differently and being able to almost be given permission to slow down and stop and just be," Scenna tells SBS News.

"It took a while to slow down and really have a city adrenaline stop, but after a couple of months we sort of went, 'actually we don't want to go to the city anymore'.

But behind the tranquillity lies a challenge shared by many of the Daintree's roughly 700 residents. Living beyond the electricity grid means finding ways to balance life in this remote rainforest with the realities of modern living.

In 2021, Scenna and her family swapped life in Sydney for the quiet of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Daintree Rainforest.

Hoping to escape the pace of city life, her family spent a year travelling around Australia before deciding they were ready for a change.

The journey led the couple to settle in the rainforest, with Scenna leaving her public sector job to run a caravan park and restaurant with her husband , Bruno.

But the dream of living among the ancient trees comes with practical challenges. Like many residents in the region, the couple must find their own solutions for powering their home and business.

While the Scennas have a hybrid energy system that includes solar, relying on diesel generators remains a necessity.

They paid about $300,000 for the solar that powers around a third of their business.

Bruno says installing enough solar panels to power their entire operation would be expensive and require clearing more rainforest for additional infrastructure.

"From an environmental perspective, why would you do that when you can have renewable energy? I fundamentally don't understand," he tells SBS News.

Growing uncertainty around fuel costs, including volatility linked to global events , has renewed calls from residents for a renewable energy solution in the Daintree.

title.en: More GPs are asking patients this question. What should you do?
title.zh: 更多全科医生正在问病人这个问题。你该怎么做？

summary.en: General practitioners are increasingly adopting a new practice during patient appointments, which is rapidly spreading. However, this new approach has not been universally accepted, with some expressing reservations.
summary.zh: 全科医生在病人就诊时正在迅速推广一项新做法。然而，并非所有人都对此信服。

body.en:
Walk into a GP's room these days, and you might be asked something new: "Do you consent to me using an AI transcription tool?"

It's a question that could soon become routine, with AI scribes now used by roughly 40 per cent of Australian GPs, up from 22 per cent in August 2024, according to survey data from the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP).

Dr Janice Tan, a spokesperson for RACGP's expert committee, said GPs and clinicians use AI scribes to transcribe conversations with patients, take automated notes, and summarise what was discussed.

"During the consult, they [the AI scribe] listen and produce a draft note afterwards," she told SBS News. "Many also draft referral and specialist letters, care plans, and sometimes a plain-English summary for the patient."

But she's clear that the software documents interactions — it doesn't decide care plans.

"A product that starts suggesting a diagnosis or treatment the clinician didn't state is no longer a scribe, and sits in a different regulatory category," she said.

But another expert said more safeguards are needed to protect patients — and the benefits aren't as clear-cut as they first appear.

For GPs, Tan said the appeal comes down to reduced burnout and more patient-centred care.

"There's less documentation after hours, which is a real driver of burnout and people leaving the profession," she said.

"The doctor is looking at you rather than the keyboard … there's more patient-centred consults, not quicker ones."

"The most underused benefit is the patient-facing summary … [which features] what we discussed, what changed, when to come back. That's valuable for anyone managing something complex, and for carers."

She also said it allows for "better and more consistent records", which are particularly helpful if you don't always see the same GP.

Andrew Cullen from the University of Melbourne's School of Computing and Information Systems agrees GPs are the clear winners — but is more cautious about what patients get out of it.

"GPs and clinicians love scribes, because they no longer need to take notes — so they can devote more time to their patients," he told SBS News. "However, for patients, the benefit is a lot less clear."

His main concern is 'hallucination' — when AI systems, including scribes, confidently make up facts. He cited a 2025 study which he said found "up to 20 per cent of notes made by AI scribes contained major errors".

title.en: The major citizenship ruling affecting Australians like Ophelia
title.zh: 影响奥菲莉亚等澳大利亚人的重大公民身份裁决

summary.en: A landmark court ruling in Australia is expected to alter the criteria and possibilities for citizenship claims for certain individuals within the country.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚一项具有里程碑意义的法院裁决，可能会重塑该国部分公民的公民身份申请条件和可能性。

body.en:
When Ophelia Bryant first travelled to Italy in 1986, she says she felt something she could not quite explain.

Her parents had been born in Italy, as had all four of her grandparents. They immigrated to Australia in 1955, where Bryant was born three years later.

Italy has remained a constant in her life, with Bryant returning more than a dozen times to visit relatives and reconnect with her family roots.

But when she began looking into whether she could formally claim Italian citizenship, she discovered her family history came with a legal complication.

Her parents became Australian citizens in 1961, when Bryant was a child, and later formally renounced their Italian citizenship.

Under a restrictive interpretation of Italy's citizenship laws, known as the 'minor issue', that could break the line of citizenship transmission.

Now, a landmark decision by Italy's highest court has changed that legal interpretation — and Bryant is "optimistic because that door may finally be open".

The so-called minor issue arose from conflicting interpretations of Italy's 1912 citizenship law.

One provision established that children born overseas to an Italian citizen could acquire Italian citizenship from birth.

Another was interpreted as meaning that when an Italian parent became a citizen of another country, their minor children could lose their Italian citizenship along with them.

That interpretation gained ground through Italian court decisions from 2023 onwards, leading to the rejection of citizenship-by-descent applications.

But in July, Italy's Supreme Court's United Sections, the court's highest panel for resolving conflicting legal interpretations, ruled that citizenship acquired at birth was not automatically lost when an Italian parent subsequently naturalised in another country.

Brisbane-based Italian lawyer Fabrizio Fiorino, who advises clients on Italian citizenship applications, said the decision effectively restores the previous interpretation of the law.

"It was not a change in a provision, but it was a change in the interpretation of rules," he said.

He told SBS News the ruling means people who were Italian citizens from birth cannot simply be considered to have lost that citizenship because their parents later became foreign citizens while they were minors.

For thousands of people whose citizenship applications were rejected on that basis, the decision could provide a pathway back.

Italy's interior ministry has since issued a letter instructing authorities to follow the Supreme Court's interpretation.
